title: Escarpment and Rivergate
premise: Odile Dunmore has spent nine years flying medicine and gossip into the interior, keeping her past sealed behind the cockpit door. When her old rival Cass Merrow buys out the airstrip's debt and forces the crew to take the one contract Odile's late father swore off—the resupply of Rivergate, a valley town cut off since the disaster that killed her brother—she must either walk away from everything she's built or fly the route that broke her. As monsoon season closes in and the escarpment passes fill with storm, Odile discovers the disaster was no accident, and that Cass's contract is a trap set by the men who caused it. In a final flight through the narrowing weather window, Odile exposes the truth, saves Rivergate's stranded winter stores, and chooses love—her partnership with mechanic Wren Adeyemi and her reclaimed place among the valley people—over the invisible life she thought was her only inheritance.
about_author: I. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former bush pilot who spent a decade flying cargo across northern ranges before trading the cockpit for the writing desk. Their fiction draws on the unforgiving geography, tight-knit airstrip communities, and moral weather of the far interior.

chapters.title: Fuel and Fog
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine medevac flight through morning fog establishes her skill, her solitude, and the airstrip town of Escarpment she calls home without quite belonging to. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the ache of a woman who has made invisibility an art.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The airstrip's owner dies and his debts pass to his daughter; Odile learns the strip itself is collateral. She reads her father's old ledger, finding the Rivergate route blacked out. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance—everything her father left her is a debt.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The airstrip mechanic rebuilds Odile's engine and their easy banter reveals a slow-burning affection neither will name. Wren notices the Rivergate pages torn from the maintenance logs. Emotional beat: warmth as counterweight to Odile's guardedness.

chapters.title: Cass Merrow Lands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cass arrives with lawyers and a contract: fly Rivergate's winter resupply or lose the strip. Nine years of rivalry and history between them crackles in every exchange. Emotional beat: the past landing hard, like a plane with no runway.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback woven through present: the Rivergate disaster nine years ago, her brother Theo's death on the escarpment pass, her father's oath never to fly it again. Emotional beat: grief surfacing like wreckage after a thaw.

chapters.title: The Crew Decides
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The pilots and ground crew vote—take the contract and keep their livelihoods, or refuse and lose the strip. Odile abstains and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: belonging tested by economics; a community splitting along fault lines.

chapters.title: Pre-Flight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren preps the old cargo plane, finding sabotage signs—drained hydraulics, a filed tie-rod—and says nothing, unsure who to trust. Emotional beat: love expressed as vigilance; the first hint someone wants this flight to fail.

chapters.title: First Leg North
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew ferries supplies to the staging town of Kettle Falls. Cass flies the second plane, and their rivalry turns into grudging professional respect over a storm cell. Emotional beat: two pilots learning the other's language.

chapters.title: Rumors at Kettle Falls
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Locals whisper that Rivergate's isolation isn't weather—it's enforced. A retired surveyor recognizes Odile's surname and goes quiet. Emotional beat: the feeling of being recognized when you've paid to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The Surveyor's Map
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The old surveyor gives Odile her father's original escarpment survey, marked with a route no one flies—and a note in Theo's handwriting. Emotional beat: inheritance as a map with a wound drawn on it.

chapters.title: Weather Window
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Satellite reports show the monsoon making landfall early; they have six days before the passes close for the season. Wren quietly fixes the sabotage and starts watching the crew. Emotional beat: the clock starting, tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Cass's Confession
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass reveals she didn't buy the debt for profit—someone paid her to force the Rivergate contract, and she's been flying the job to find out who. Emotional beat: rivalry reframed as two people trapped in the same snare.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Approach
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. First attempt at the pass; downdrafts and memory hit Odile equally hard. She turns back at the exact point where Theo's plane went down. Emotional beat: courage failing at the precise coordinates of grief.

chapters.title: Rivergate on the Radio
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A faint radio call from Rivergate: the town's medicine stores are gone, a fever is spreading, and the winter road is already snowed shut. Emotional beat: duty arriving as a human voice, not an abstraction.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Someone reports the plane's paperwork falsified; authorities ground them at Kettle Falls. Wren traces the complaint to a shell company with familiar initials. Emotional beat: fury and protectiveness; the conspiracy shows its hand.

chapters.title: What Theo Found
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Decoding Theo's note and the survey: the original disaster was caused by a blasting company's illegal mine above the pass, and the men who ran it are now Rivergate's supposed benefactors. Emotional beat: grief converting to purpose.

chapters.title: Night Flight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Cass fly a medicine run at night through the storm's leading edge, trading confidences across the headset. Emotional beat: rivalry dissolving into sisterhood at altitude.

chapters.title: The Strip at Rivergate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They land in the valley town her family swore off; the people remember her father, and some blame him for the crash. Emotional beat: belonging offered and refused in the same handshake.

chapters.title: The Fever Ward
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile helps the town's nurse, Mara, and sees the cost of nine years of silence—the medicine that never came. Emotional beat: shame metabolized into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren Comes North
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren defies the grounding order, ferries the plane north through weather that should be unflyable, and lands half-broke and furious. Emotional beat: love as a decision made in bad weather.

chapters.title: The Mine Above
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Cass hike to the abandoned mine and find it isn't abandoned—new blasting has destabilized the escarpment, and the next slide will bury Rivergate's water source. Emotional beat: the past is not past; it is actively collapsing.

chapters.title: The Men Who Paid
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass names the principals: the Halvard Group, which bought the debt, hired her, and has been buying Rivergate's land cheap since the disaster. Emotional beat: the trap's full shape revealed—Odile was the perfect deniable pilot.

chapters.title: Sabotage, Second Round
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Halvard man at the staging town torches their spare engine and takes the radio codes. Wren is injured stopping him. Emotional beat: the cost of staying visible; Odile forced to choose between the mission and Wren.

chapters.title: Bedside
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Wren's recovery; Odile finally says out loud what she's been flying away from for nine years. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly, duty winning for now—but barely.

chapters.title: The Town Votes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Rivergate learns the truth about the mine and must decide: evacuate through the pass before the monsoon, or stay and fight for the valley. Emotional beat: a community choosing courage over safety, mirroring Odile's arc.

chapters.title: Evacuation Math
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The planes can move maybe two hundred people before the passes close; the town has four hundred. Every load is a triage decision. Emotional beat: the arithmetic of conscience; Odile refusing to play God, then having to.

chapters.title: Halvard's Offer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Halvard representative offers Odile everything: the strip's deed, her father's debts cleared, Theo's name cleared—if she flies the evacuation and says nothing about the mine. Emotional beat: temptation wearing the face of justice.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile declines, publicly, at the airstrip, with the town listening. Halvard's man promises the weather will bury the evidence. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility dies; she chooses to be seen.

chapters.title: Loading the First Wave
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The evacuation begins—elderly, sick, children first—through worsening weather. Wren runs the strip like a conductor while Odile flies shuttle runs. Emotional beat: exhausted grace; a community becoming a machine of mercy.

chapters.title: The Slide Begins
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The escarpment starts to go early; a rockfall seals the upper pass with half the town still below. Emotional beat: nature calling in its debt; the plan dying in real time.

chapters.title: The Route No One Flies
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile realizes her father's marked route—the impossible one, the one that killed Theo—may be the only way out over the range ahead of the monsoon. Emotional beat: inheritance as a dare; the map's wound becoming a door.

chapters.title: Reading Theo's Log
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile finally reads her brother's flight log all the way through and finds he died mapping a safe corridor, not flying recklessly—the crash was Halvard's blasting, and his route is sound. Emotional beat: the brother restored to her; grief rewritten.

chapters.title: Cass Takes the Lead Plane
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass volunteers to fly the route first, proving it with her own life, settling nine years of rivalry in one sentence. Emotional beat: rivalry transmuted into sacrifice and trust.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The first wave crosses the escarpment through Theo's corridor as the monsoon's edge arrives—whiteout, downdraft, the mountain forgiving nothing. Emotional beat: terror and transcendence; the flight of her life in her brother's shadow.

chapters.title: The Second Wave
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Odile and Cass fly the corridor again and again until the last load; Wren holds the strip through rising water. Emotional beat: repetition as redemption; every safe landing a small resurrection.

chapters.title: The Evidence Flight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the final crossing, Odile carries not people but proof—survey data, mine records, Theo's log—straight to the provincial capital, flying through the storm's teeth to beat Halvard's lawyers. Emotional beat: duty and love finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The evidence lands; Halvard's operation unravels as the mine's records go public and Rivergate's land titles are voided. Emotional beat: justice arriving not as lightning but as paperwork, and being no less satisfying.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Back in Rivergate, the town buries its dead from the original disaster properly, and Odile adds Theo's name to the memorial with her own hands. Emotional beat: grief given its ceremony at last.

chapters.title: Deeds and Debts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The airstrip at Escarpment is secured, the crew reunited, and Cass—now a partner, not a rival—proposes they fly the Rivergate route as a permanent supply line. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed and rewritten; belonging chosen.

chapters.title: Escarpment and Rivergate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Spring: Odile and Wren fly the first run of the new season together, the range green and forgiving for once. Odile finally understands her inheritance was never the debt or the oath—it was the sky and the people worth flying it for. Emotional beat: arrival; love and duty reconciled in level flight.
